performed_via_github_app.description:
Codecov provides highly integrated tools to group, merge, archive and compare coverage reports. Whether your team is comparing changes in a pull request or reviewing a single commit, Codecov will improve the code review workflow and quality.

## Code coverage done right.®

1. Upload coverage reports from your CI builds.
2. Codecov merges all builds and languages into one beautiful coherent report.
3. Get commit statuses, pull request comments and coverage overlay via our browser extension.

When Codecov merges your uploads it keeps track of the CI provider (inc. build details) and user specified context, e.g. `#unittest` ~ `#smoketest` or `#oldcode` ~ `#newcode`. You can track the `#unittest` coverage independently of other groups. [Learn more here](
http://docs.codecov.io/docs/flags)

Through **Codecov's Browser Extension** reports overlay directly in GitHub UI to assist in code review in [Chrome](https://chrome.google.com/webstore/detail/codecov/gedikamndpbemklijjkncpnolildpbgo) or Firefox (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/codecov/)

*Highly detailed* **pull request comments** and *customizable* **commit statuses** will improve your team's workflow and code coverage incrementally.

**File backed configuration** all through the `codecov.yml`. 

## FAQ
- Do you **merge multiple uploads** to the same commit? **Yes**
- Do you **support multiple languages** in the same project? **Yes**
- Can you **group coverage reports** by project and/or test type? **Yes**
- How does **pricing** work? Only paid users can view reports and post statuses/comments.

body:
## Licensing plan for Strudel integration

Strudel is **AGPL-3.0-or-later** with no linking exception, so we need to be deliberate about how it's wired up. Summarizing where we landed.

### The constraint

As written, this branch loads `@strudel/web` from unpkg and calls `initStrudel`/`setPattern` through `Js.Unsafe` — Hazel's code calling Strudel's functions and passing its objects inside one JS execution context. That's a combined work, and lazy-loading the script tag doesn't change it: per the [GPL FAQ](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.en.html), dynamically linked plug-ins that "make function calls to each other and share data structures" form a single program. So the main dev build would have to ship as AGPL-3.0 — which we don't want, since Hazel's permissive license is load-bearing for downstream research use and forks.

### The plan

1. **Frame-side adapter, AGPL-3.0.** A small module wrapping `@strudel/repl` (bump 1.0.3 → 1.3.0) that owns all Strudel API contact: scheduler, pattern eval, sample loading. Lives in this repo under its own `LICENSE`.
2. **Loaded as a separate document from the same build.** `<iframe src="strudel/index.html">`, same origin, same output directory — one `make serve`, no second process, works from a fresh clone with the network unplugged.
3. **Hazel-side client, MIT.** Communicates by `postMessage` only (`{type:'eval', code}` / `{type:'stop'}`), never by reaching into the frame. Enforced with a lint rule banning `contentWindow`/`contentDocument` from Hazel-side code, so nothing couples through it later by accident.

Music examples ship in the main dev build; only the adapter is AGPL.

### Why this keeps Hazel MIT

AGPL §5's aggregate clause exempts "separate and independent works... not combined with [the covered work] such as to form a larger program," and the FSF's test is the intimacy of communication — "pipes, sockets and command-line arguments are communication mechanisms normally used between two separate programs." A separate browser document exchanging serialized messages is the direct analog: we pass pattern code across, never shared objects or function calls. Hazel's MIT files stay MIT, and no contributor re-licensing is needed either way, since MIT already permits sublicensing.

### Obligations

Both cheap, since we publish sources anyway. Preserve Strudel's notices and `LICENSE`, and don't let the bundler strip headers or tree-shake Strudel into a shared chunk with the js_of_ocaml output. And provide Corresponding Source for the copy we serve — §6(d) allows hosting it elsewhere given "clear directions next to the object code," so a link to codeberg.org/uzu/strudel **pinned to the exact version**, plus our build config, is enough.

### Open issue: samples

The bigger practical problem, and not a copyleft one. `prebake()` hardcodes sample banks on `raw.githubusercontent.com`, and the PWA caching that makes strudel.cc work offline lives in the site, not the npm package — so we need our own prebake registering local banks.

A network-free clone means committing audio, and full VCSL/Dirt-Samples is far too large for Hazel's history. Proposal: commit a curated few-MB CC0 subset so the doc examples make sound offline, with `make setup-samples` fetching the full banks on demand. That also settles licensing diligence, since sample licenses are mixed and independent of AGPL (VCSL is CC0, Salamander piano CC-BY, mridangam CC-BY-SA, Dirt-Samples unstated in `dough-samples`) and a small curated set is one we can actually verify.
